chunks.arabic_text: عَلَلُ الشَّرَائِعِ: أَبِي، عَن سَعْدٍ، عَن مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْوَلِيدِ وَالسِّنْدِيِّ، عَن أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ، عَن مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ وَحُرَيْزٍ، عَن أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامِ قَالَ

translations.en: Ilal al-Shara'i: My father, from Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid and al-Sindi, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Bashir and Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لَهُ: إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ شَيْئًا أَشَدَّ عَلَيَّ مِنْ اخْتِلَافِ أَصْحَابِنَا، قَالَ: ذَلِكَ مِنِّي

translations.en: I said to him: There is nothing more difficult for me than the differences among our companions, he said: That is from me.

en.summary: Hariz narrates to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) that he finds the disagreements among their followers to be the most difficult burden for him. The Imam responds that these differences were intentionally caused by him (the Imam) as a test or means of distinction.
en.seo_question: Why did the Imams cause differences among their followers?

key_terms.مِنِّي: From me (indicating agency of the Imam)
